--- title: "[Graph.add_turan_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a Turán graph T(n, r) to the current graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L5362-L5454){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_turan_graph( n, r, type=None, label=True, rel=None, part_attr="part", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Turán graph](/assets/graphs/add-turan-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three Turán graphs on a ring of seven nodes for r=2, 3, and 4 parts, each part in its own color. The seven nodes are split into parts as equal as possible (4 and 3; 3, 2, and 2; 2, 2, 2, and 1) and every pair of nodes in different parts is joined, so the graph gains edges as r grows (12, 16, and 18)." width="100%"} The Turán graph splits `n` nodes into `r` groups whose sizes differ by at most one and joins every pair of nodes in different groups. It is the complete multipartite graph with the most edges among all graphs on `n` nodes that contain no clique of `r + 1` nodes; Turán's theorem says no `K(r+1)`-free graph on `n` nodes has more edges. The smaller groups (`n // r` nodes) come first and the larger ones (`n // r + 1` nodes) last, each as a consecutive run of node IDs, and each node's group index is stored in the `part_attr=` node attribute. In a directed graph every edge points from the earlier-created node to the later one. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Turán graphs are useful for: - extremal graph theory: they are the densest graphs without a `K(r+1)` clique - test cases for clique, coloring, and independent-set algorithms (the clique number and chromatic number are both `r` when `n >= r`) - balanced "everyone except your own group" relations, such as matches between equal teams ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Total number of nodes. Must be at least `1`. [r]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of groups. Must satisfy `1 <= r <= n`. `r=1` gives `n` isolated nodes and `r=n` gives the complete graph. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. [part_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["part"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that records each node's group index. Default is `"part"`. Pass `None` to skip storing it. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `n=` is less than `1`, or `r=` is not between `1` and `n=`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} `T(7, 3)` splits seven nodes into groups of `2`, `2`, and `3`: ::: {#00a105b3 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_turan_graph(n=7, r=3) graph.get_node_df()["part"].value_counts().sort("part") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: It has the most edges a seven-node graph can have without containing four mutually joined nodes, and its largest clique has exactly `r=3` nodes: ::: {#62aa08a0 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.count_edges(), graph.clique_number() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (16, 3) ``` ::: :::
